title: My God, What Inward Grief I Feel
description: My God, What Inward Grief I Feel in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 139, part 3, headed “Sincerity professed, and grace tried; or, The heart- searching of God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, what in-ward grief I feel When im-pious men trans-gress thy will! I mourn to hear their lips pro-fane Take thy tre-men-dous Name in vain.

lines: My God, what inward grief I feel
When impious men transgress thy will!
I mourn to hear their lips profane
Take thy tremendous Name in vain.
Does not my soul detest and hate
The sons of malice and deceit?
Those that oppose thy laws and thee
I count them enemies to me.
Lord, search my soul, try every thought;
Tho' my own heart accuse me not
Of walking in a false disguise,
I beg the trial of thine eyes.
Do I indulge some unknown sin?
O turn my feet whene'er I stray,
And lead me in thy perfect way.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
